what_happened: Scene: white kettle on the counter right of a dark 4-burner gas range (frying pan at the rear). Stage 0 was fine: grasp 96, lift 0.109 m, released at 169 on a burner on the RIGHT half of the range, 0.13 m from its centre. Stage 0 complete at 191 (fast). Stage 1: 280-340 the gripper went to the front knob panel and took the LEFT-most knob, turning it 340-392 (0.30 at 384, 0.47 at 416). A blue flame appears on the REAR-LEFT burner at ~392, while the kettle sits on the right. 480-512 it turned the same knob further (1.32 rad by 528) and let go at 515. Then it wandered: 528-568 low in front of the cabinet drawers, 600-1000 up and to the right (wrist sees counters, microwave, wall). It never touched the right-hand knobs, and the kettle's burner stayed off.
causal_chain: kettle placed on a right-hand burner (169) -> policy turned the left-most knob = rear_left burner (340-512, 1.32 rad) -> wrong burner lit; stage 1 needs the burner under the kettle -> wandered 515-1000 without correcting -> fail
self_recovery: none: after turning the wrong knob it never looked at or touched another knob.
official_criterion_notes: fixtures.stage1:stove.done_intervals [[386,1000]] say 'done' because the fixture value is the max over all knobs; stage 1 itself correctly never holds. The packet does not say which burner the kettle is on, so the wrong burner had to be read from the flame in the video.
uncertain_about: The exact name of the kettle's burner (front_right vs rear_right): the kettle is 0.13 m from the nearest burner centre, close to the 0.15 m threshold.
